title: Enforcement Decree of the Requisition Act
full_text:
ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE REQUISITION ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Requisition Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Requisition Officers)
"Persons prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 3(2) of the Requisition Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means any of the following persons: <Amended Sept. 5, 2017>
1. Commanders holding the rank of general officer;
2. Field-grade commanders who are the heads of units belonging to formations at corps level or above and conducting independent operations.

Article 3 (Issuance of Requisition Warrants)
Where a requisition officer deems it necessary for issuing a requisition warrant under Article 7(1) of the Act, the officer may require the head of a unit requesting the object of requisition to submit an application for requisition in advance.

Article 4 (Scope of Expenses Borne by the State)
Expenses borne by the State under Articles 9(2) and 16(4) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Movable property: Expenses for transportation to the designated place and packing;
2. Immovable property and rights: Expenses incurred in handing over possession or otherwise delivering such property or rights.

Article 5 (Investigation of the Condition of Objects of Requisition)
① An investigation of objects of requisition under Article 12(1) of the Act shall include the following matters: <Amended Aug. 31, 2016>
1. Condition:
The shape, purpose of use, types and quantities of things situated on the land [including crops, buildings, artificial structures, standing trees, and graves], and reference information indicating the condition of the requisitioned objects (where the condition is difficult to record, photographs shall be attached);
2. Officially assessed land price or market price:
(a) Land: The individually assessed public land price published under Article 10 of the Act on the Public Announcement of Real Estate Values;
(b) Buildings: The publicly announced price or market price under the Act on the Public Announcement of Real Estate Values;
(c) Movable property: Market price.
② Before receiving an object for execution from a requisition execution officer, a requisition officer may require the execution officer to investigate the object under Article 12(1) of the Act in advance.

Article 6 (Reissuance of Certificates of Requisition)
Where a certificate of requisition becomes unusable or is lost, the owner, possessor, or manager of the object of requisition (hereinafter referred to as a "person subject to requisition") shall apply for reissuance without delay, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.

Article 7 (Procedures for Release from Requisition)
① Where a requisition officer intends to release an object from requisition under Article 15(1) of the Act, the officer shall in advance require the head of the unit using the requisitioned object to investigate its shape, publicly assessed land price, price, and other necessary matters and to submit the findings.
② Where a notice of inability to return a requisitioned object is issued under the proviso to Article 16(1) of the Act, the requisition shall be deemed released. In such cases, neither the notice of release from requisition nor the certificate of release from requisition under the main sentence of Article 16(1) of the Act shall be issued.

Article 8 (Consultation on Purchase of Requisitioned Objects)
① Where a person subject to requisition intends to consult with the Minister of National Defense on the purchase of a requisitioned object under Article 15(2) of the Act, the person shall submit documents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of National Defense.
② Within six months after receiving a request for consultation on purchasing a requisitioned object, the Minister of National Defense shall notify the person who requested consultation whether the object is eligible for purchase and the estimated purchase price, among other matters.

Article 9 (Preliminary Investigation of Objects of Requisition)
① Where the Minister of National Defense conducts a preliminary investigation of objects of requisition under Article 17(1) of the Act, the Minister shall notify the relevant person subject to requisition of the date, time, and place of the investigation and other necessary matters at least 30 days before the investigation date.
② A person subject to requisition notified under paragraph ① may participate in the investigation and state opinions; if the person considers the date, time, or place of the investigation notified by the Minister of National Defense inappropriate, the person may apply for a change at least 15 days before the investigation date.
③ Upon receipt of an application for a change under paragraph ②, the Minister of National Defense shall decide whether to make the change within ten days after receipt and notify the applicant in writing.
④ A public official conducting a preliminary investigation of objects of requisition under Article 17(1) of the Act shall present identification indicating the official's status to the person subject to requisition.

Article 10 (Determination of Amounts of Compensation)
The amount of compensation payable under Article 19 of the Act shall be assessed and determined by the Requisition Compensation Deliberation Committee under Article 24(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Deliberation Committee"), taking into account the compensation standards under Article 12 of this Decree.

Article 11 (Rate of Interest on Delayed Payment)
"An interest rate not lower than the statutory rate prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso to Article 19(5) of the Act means eight percent per annum.

Article 12 (Compensation Standards)
Details of the compensation standards determined under Article 21(1) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended Aug. 31, 2016; Nov. 1, 2016; Jan. 21, 2022>
1. Compensation for immovable property (including destroyed immovable property), rights, and non-consumable movable property shall be based on the value appraised by an appraisal corporation, etc. under the Act on Appraisal and Certified Appraisers;
2. Compensation for consumable movable property shall be based on its market price at the time of requisition;
3. Compensation for destroyed non-consumable movable property shall be based on its market price at the time of destruction.

Article 13 (Public Announcement of Implementation of Compensation)
The Minister of National Defense shall announce the following matters, at least 30 days before the commencement date for claiming compensation, through at least one of a daily newspaper, the Official Gazette, an official bulletin, a bulletin board of the local government having jurisdiction over the location of the object of requisition, or broadcasting, and shall also publish the announcement on an Internet website, under Article 22 of the Act: <Amended Nov. 24, 2020>
1. Persons and scope eligible for payment of compensation;
2. Eligibility of persons claiming compensation;
3. Period and place for receipt of claims for compensation;
4. Application procedures and required documents;
5. Procedures for payment of compensation;
6. Other matters concerning payment of compensation.

Article 14 (Payment of Compensation in Securities)
① The face value of requisition compensation securities (hereinafter referred to as "securities") paid under Article 22-2(1) of the Act shall be 100,000 won.
② Securities shall be redeemed in equal installments over five years after a one-year grace period from their date of issue, and the interest rate on the amount to be redeemed shall be eight percent per annum.

Article 15 (Deposit)
"The period prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the former part of Article 22-4(1) of the Act means 90 days after the date of receipt of a notice of payment of requisition compensation under Articles 22(2) and 24(4) of the Act.

Article 16 (Composition of Deliberation Committee)
① The Deliberation Committee shall consist of not more than 15 members, including one chairperson and one vice chairperson.
② The Vice Minister of National Defense shall serve as chairperson of the Deliberation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "chairperson"), and the Vice Minister's Assistant for National Defense shall serve as vice chairperson. <Amended July 25, 2023; Jan. 2, 2026>
③ The Minister of National Defense shall appoint members from among general-service public officials belonging to the Senior Civil Service (including equivalent special-service and political-service public officials) of the Ministry of Finance and Economy, Ministry of Justice, Ministry of National Defense, Ministry of the Interior and Safety, Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs, Ministry of Health and Welfare, and Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, and general officers or field-grade officers of the Army, Navy, and Air Force; and shall commission members from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience in property valuation. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Nov. 19, 2014; July 26, 2017; Sept. 5, 2017; Dec. 30, 2025>

Article 17 (Duties)
① The chairperson shall represent the Deliberation Committee and exercise overall control over its business.
② Where the chairperson is unable to perform the duties due to unavoidable circumstances, the vice chairperson shall act on behalf of the chairperson; where both the chairperson and vice chairperson are unable to perform those duties due to unavoidable circumstances, a member designated in advance by the chairperson shall act on behalf of the chairperson.

Article 18 (Meetings)
① The chairperson shall convene meetings of the Deliberation Committee and preside over them.
② A meeting of the Deliberation Committee shall adopt resolutions with the attendance of a majority of all incumbent members and the affirmative votes of a majority of the members present.

Article 19 (Hearing Opinions)
① Where the chairperson deems it necessary, the chairperson may have a public official responsible for requisition compensation affairs attend a meeting of the Deliberation Committee and present opinions.
② When deliberating on a request for reexamination under Article 24(3) of the Act, the Deliberation Committee shall have the applicant attend a meeting and hear their opinions: Provided, That this shall not apply if the applicant submits a written opinion or, without justifiable grounds, fails to comply with at least two requests to attend a meeting of the Deliberation Committee.

Article 20 (Administrative Secretary)
① The Deliberation Committee shall have one administrative secretary to handle its administrative affairs.
② The administrative secretary shall be designated by the Minister of National Defense from among public officials affiliated with the Ministry of National Defense.

Article 21 (Detailed Operational Rules)
Matters necessary for the operation of the Deliberation Committee other than those prescribed in this Decree shall be determined by the chairperson following a resolution of the Deliberation Committee.

Article 22 (Requests for Reexamination)
① A request for reexamination under Article 24(3) of the Act shall be submitted in writing within 20 days after receipt of a notice of payment of requisition compensation under Article 22(2) of the Act, stating:
1. Name, address, and contact information of the applicant;
2. Respondent;
3. Purport of and grounds for the request.
② The Deliberation Committee may require the applicant or respondent to submit materials or information necessary for examination, and the applicant or respondent shall submit such materials or information immediately unless there are special circumstances.
③ The Deliberation Committee may, ex officio or upon application, require an applicant, respondent, interested party, or other relevant person to attend the Committee and make a statement.
④ Where deemed necessary, the Deliberation Committee may have experts or other persons attend as witnesses for reference or may hear their written opinions.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 22272, July 12, 2010>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Repeal of Another Decree)
The Regulations on the Requisition Compensation Deliberation Committee are hereby repealed.

Article 3 (Relationship to Other Statutes)
Where another statute or regulation cites the former Enforcement Decree of the Requisition Act, the former Regulations on the Requisition Compensation Deliberation Committee, or any provision thereof at the time this Decree enters into force, and this Decree contains a corresponding provision, the citation shall be deemed to refer to this Decree or the corresponding provision thereof in place of the former Decree, Regulations, or provision.
